name: Elasticsearch
description: Elasticsearch cluster reads: cluster health and stats, the index list, one index's settings and mappings, a document count, and a query-string search. Read-only; no index, document, mapping or cluster-setting write is wired here.

tools.name: cluster_health
tools.description: Get Elasticsearch cluster health: green/yellow/red status, node counts and shard allocation

tools.name: cluster_stats
tools.description: Get Elasticsearch cluster statistics: index count, document count, store size, node count and versions

tools.name: list_indices
tools.description: List the indices on the cluster with health, status, shard counts and document counts

tools.name: get_index
tools.description: Get one index's aliases, mappings and settings

tools.name: count_documents
tools.description: Count the documents in one index, optionally matching a Lucene query string

index.description: Index name to count documents in

q.description: Optional Lucene query string; omit to count every document

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search one index with a Lucene query string and return the matching documents

q.description: Lucene query string, e.g. status:error AND host:web01; omit to match every document

size.description: Max documents to return (default 10, capped at 50 by this connector)

sort.description: Optional sort clause, e.g. @timestamp:desc (the field must be sortable)

needs_review: AUTH CHANGED FROM THE SCAFFOLD, DELIBERATELY: the scaffold wrote {type: header, header: Authorization, template: 'ApiKey {{api_key}}'} because it took the first credential field it found. The vault entry (integrationTypeRegistry.elasticsearch) supports BOTH forms in testHeaders: 'ApiKey <api_key>' when api_key is present, otherwise base64(username:password) as HTTP Basic. Elasticsearch documents both as first-class (Authenticate with HTTP basic auth / API keys, https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/security-api-authenticate.html). Basic auth with the built-in 'elastic' superuser is what a fresh cluster has BEFORE anyone mints an API key, so it is what the live harness can drive against an ephemeral container. auth is therefore {type: basic, userField: username, passField: password}, matching the vault's own fallback branch byte for byte. An api_key variant of this spec stays an unbuilt gap rather than a silent one.

REQUIREDFIELDS ARE NARROWER THAN THE VAULT FORM, ON PURPOSE: the vault marks every field optional (cloud_id, host, api_key, username, password) and enforces 'either Cloud ID or Host URL' in validateCredentials. A spec cannot express 'one of', so it declares the combination this connector actually uses: host + username + password. cloud_id is NOT supported here (an Elastic Cloud ID has to be decoded into a host before any request can be built, which the declarative runtime cannot do), so Elastic Cloud customers must supply the deployment's host URL.

BASE URL IS CUSTOMER-SUPPLIED, SO NOTHING HERE IS PROVABLE BLIND: base_url is {fromCredential: 'host'} and Elasticsearch is self-hosted or per-deployment, so there is no vendor-run host to shape-prove against. This spec is NOT SHAPE_PROVEN by a blind 401 sweep; it is marked for the live harness, which stands up an ephemeral Elasticsearch container with an index named 'quoxproof-live' and drives every tool against it.

CATEGORY FOLLOWS THE TAXONOMY, NOT THE SCAFFOLD GUESS: the scaffold wrote 'uncategorized', which is not one of the twelve values in use across this spec directory (cloud_hosting, commerce_finance, communication, crm_sales, data_ai, developer, files_knowledge, hr_hiring, marketing_email, media, monitoring, project_management) and the vault entry carries no category at all. 'data_ai' is used: Elasticsearch sits with the other datastores and search/vector engines already filed there (pinecone, upstash, singlestore, neon, planetscale, turso, confluent). 'monitoring' was rejected because this connector reads a datastore, it does not watch a system.

PROBES RESOLVE ON A FRESH CLUSTER: cluster_health, cluster_stats and list_indices need no index and carry an empty _probe. get_index, count_documents and search probe input.index='quoxproof-live', the exact index name the live provisioner creates; search probes q='*' and size=5 so it returns a well-formed zero-hit body on an empty index rather than depending on a document existing.

LIST_INDICES AND GET_INDEX INTENTIONALLY HAVE NO PICK: _cat/indices returns a top-level array whose keys are LITERALLY dotted ('docs.count', 'store.size'), and this runtime resolves a pick source as a dotted PATH (declarativeRuntime.getPath splits on '.'), so picking them would silently yield undefined. The column set is trimmed with the documented h parameter instead, which is lossless for the fields named. GET /{index} keys its body by the index NAME, which is dynamic, so no static pick can address it. Both rely on truncate 2000 alone.

SIZE CLAMP IS OURS, NOT ELASTICSEARCH'S: the search API's own default is size=10 with index.max_result_window (default 10000) as the real ceiling. The 10/50 clamp is a connector-side guard so an agent cannot pull a huge result page through a tool call, and the input description says so rather than implying Elasticsearch rejects 51. track_total_hits=true is sent so the reported total is exact rather than the default 10000 cap.

READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THE OMISSIONS ARE THE POINT: all six tools are GETs. The same REST surface exposes index creation and deletion, document index/update/delete, _bulk, reindex, mapping and cluster-setting writes, and the whole security API (users, roles, API keys). None is wired here. Nothing in this connector may be described as managing an Elasticsearch cluster.

RESPONSE SHAPES COME FROM THE REFERENCE BODIES: cluster_health picks the documented fields of the cluster health response (cluster_name, status, timed_out, number_of_nodes, number_of_data_nodes, active_primary_shards, active_shards, relocating_shards, initializing_shards, unassigned_shards, active_shards_percent_as_number); cluster_stats picks the nested indices.count / indices.docs.count / indices.docs.deleted / indices.store.size_in_bytes / indices.shards.total / nodes.count.total / nodes.versions; _count answers {count, _shards{total,successful,skipped,failed}}; _search answers {took, timed_out, hits{total{value,relation}, max_score, hits[{_index,_id,_score,_source}]}}. The live harness is what confirms these against a real cluster version.
